payload.title: How to Plan a Santorini Wedding Step by Step
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, who have decided Santorini is the place (or very nearly) and now need the order of decisions: legal or symbolic, which season, which kind of setting, how many guests the island can actually hold for them, how everyone gets there and what paperwork to start. They want one calm, confident plan they can work through before they spend time on individual venue enquiries.
payload.goal: Book a Wedded Concierge consultation (speak with a Wedded Advisor) at /wonderland-concierge.
payload.angle: Page-one results for 'santorini wedding' are venue lists and package pages that assume the decisions are already made. This guide is the plan itself: nine numbered steps in the order an Australian couple has to take them, starting with the one that shapes everything else (legal or symbolic, and where the legal step happens), then season from official weather data and Smartraveller advice, setting and venue type with only 4 to 6 short, verified venue examples, guest numbers against capacity and rooms, guest travel from official airport and port sources, documents as at November 2026, house rules written as questions to get in writing, the weekend around the wedding, and a booking checklist. Confident, step-led and figure-free, so it stays true and hands the venue-list intent to the venue guides.
outline_spine: Step 1: Decide legal or symbolic, and where the legal step happens (Greece or at home), in brief; link the Greece and Paros guides' legal sections.

Step 2: Pick your season (official weather data, each figure labelled by station from hnms.gr; Smartraveller heat, wildfire and wind advice dated once as at November 2026; no best month stated as fact).

Step 3: Choose the setting and venue type (caldera, beach, estate or winery, hotel, private villa) with 4 to 6 venue examples, one or two lines each; link the old live page /7-must-see-santorini-destination-wedding-venues once and /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues; primary Concierge CTA after this step.
Step 4: Size the guest list against capacity and guest rooms ('Not published' where a venue does not state it).
Step 5: Plan guest travel (Santorini airport and port from official sources; step-free access and transfers written as questions to ask, no claims, no transfer arrangements offered).

Step 6: Gather your documents (CNI, apostille, translation) from the Australian Embassy Athens and Smartraveller as at November 2026; Municipality of Thira civil steps only if an official page is read live, otherwise 'check with the municipality and the embassy, including any fees'; nothing on church or religious paperwork.
Step 7: Lock in house rules in writing (music times, exclusive use, ceremony times, suppliers, weather plan), each as a question to ask the venue.
Step 8: Plan the weekend (welcome and recovery events as ideas only, no supplier names; link /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions once).
Step 9: Your booking checklist (collects every 'not published' item and every question raised above).
What shapes the cost: a short paragraph with no figures, only if SEO confirms cost intent; link /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages.
Close: plan your Santorini wedding with a Wedded Advisor (closing CTA).
must_include: Direct answer in the first 100 words: planning a Santorini wedding comes down to a short run of decisions in order (legal or symbolic, season, setting, guest numbers, guest travel, documents, house rules, the weekend), and this guide takes them step by step; link the Greece hub /destinations/europe/greece.
Exactly 4 Key takeaways, each one concise sentence, no figures, no prices.
The nine numbered steps from 00-input as the H2 spine (see outline_spine), headings in sentence case with no pasted or bracketed keywords.
4 to 6 venue examples in step 3 only, one or two lines each, each verified by a live read of the venue's own official site saying it hosts weddings; no capacity tables, no prices, no contact details.
Weather only from official sources labelled by station; Smartraveller heat, wildfire and wind advice dated once as at November 2026.
Documents step as at November 2026 from the Australian Embassy Athens and Smartraveller; Municipality of Thira only if read live; no fees stated.

Overlap handling: /7-must-see-santorini-destination-wedding-venues linked exactly once (step 3); venue-list intent left to the venue guides (/destination-weddings/greece-wedding-venues, mykonos and paros venue guides); /venue/rocabella-santorini-hotel-spa NOT linked.

One Wedded Advisor line in the body (after step 3, primary CTA) plus the close; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md (one Wedded Advisor as a single point of contact, works in your time zone and quotes in AUD, fee agreed in writing before work begins, inclusions confirmed in writing, plans venue, travel, vendors and payments); FAQ 5 to 6; /magazine linked once as the magnet.
avoid: Any price, fee, euro or AUD figure, 'from' price, amount or percentage anywhere, including FAQ, meta and takeaways.
Turning the guide into a venue list: no more than 6 venues, no venue beyond the verified examples, no rankings or 'best'.
Linking /venue/rocabella-santorini-hotel-spa (its domain is for sale); linking the old venues page more than once.

Research talk in copy (what we could or could not find, trace or confirm; sources or method; 'on its own site', 'in its own words', 'does not publish' as our search; page dates as source talk; myths); per-line source credits; hedge stacking; 'often told' more than once.
A best month stated as fact; weather claims not from an official source.
Anything on legal, church or religious paperwork beyond the documents step; any Advisor role in paperwork; transfer arrangements; Wedded Privileges.
Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; 'from first idea to the last dance' or 'last dance' anywhere.
Vendor names other than the venue examples (no planners, photographers, florists, boats, caterers); venue contact or business details; implied partnerships.
Competitor wedding sites, directories, planner blogs, booking sites, review sites or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording, claims or images.
Cliches, exclamation marks, pasted or bracketed keywords in headings, em dashes, US spelling.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding.

This post owns the planning intent (santorini wedding, getting married in santorini, santorini wedding planning). SEO to check rankings for the variants (santorini wedding venues, santorini wedding cost, santorini wedding packages) and recommend the split in the run report.
payload.intro_plan: Open on the reader's position (Santorini is the choice, now they need the order of decisions), give the direct answer in the first 100 words, then link the Greece hub.
payload.key_takeaways_rule: Exactly 4 bullets, each a single concise sentence stating a concrete decision or fact, no figures, no prices, no research talk.
key_takeaways_plan: Decide first whether your Santorini ceremony will be legal or symbolic, because that choice sets your documents, timeline and venue options.
Choose your season from official weather data and current travel advice rather than photographs, and plan ceremony times around the heat and wind.
Match the setting to your guest list, since caldera terraces, beaches, estates and private villas differ widely in capacity and guest rooms.
Put every house rule in writing before you sign, including music times, exclusive use, ceremony times and the plan if the weather turns.
